claim_support.claim: Grounded generation can select concise source spans before generating locally attributed text.
claim_support.evidence: Abstract and method description, PDF pp. 2-3: source-span selection, sentence-level planning, and sequential sentence generation are separate steps. Supports a reading-before-summary design rationale; it does not establish CyberCase implements that three-step algorithm.

claim_support.claim: Source attribution should be evaluated as whether identifiable source material supports a generated statement.
claim_support.evidence: Abstract: AIS defines attribution against a provided independent source and a two-stage human annotation protocol. Supports distinguishing source support from real-world truth; literal quote matching alone does not implement AIS evaluation.

claim_support.claim: Citation evaluation should distinguish statement support coverage from irrelevant citations and answer correctness.
claim_support.evidence: PDF section 3.3, p. 4; human evaluation p. 8: citation recall tests support from cited passages, while citation precision tests relevance of citations. This is semantic evaluation, beyond locating a quote string.

claim_support.claim: Long-form factual precision can be assessed at the level of supported atomic facts.
claim_support.evidence: Abstract: decompose generations into atomic facts and measure the fraction supported by a reliable knowledge source. The original biography task and retrieval verifier require adaptation to a closed case-source registry.

claim_support.claim: Fluent abstractive summaries can contain content that is unfaithful to their input documents.
claim_support.evidence: Abstract: human evaluation of summarization hallucinations and comparison of entailment-based measures with standard overlap metrics. Does not quantify current CyberCase or current-model error rates.

claim_support.claim: Summary coverage should be evaluated with explicit atomic units from reference content and a constrained annotation protocol.
claim_support.evidence: PDF section 3, pp. 3-4: reference-based Atomic Content Units for summary salience, writing units and matching them to system summaries. Supports coverage evaluation, not a standalone factuality metric.

claim_support.claim: A case-review assistant can ground recommendations in source quotes verified before the final LLM generation.
claim_support.evidence: arXiv 2607.01256v1, Default Assistant Implementation / Cited Generation, p. 5: retrieve pages, extract quotes/tables, relocate and replace with directly copied spans, pass only located spans to generation. Human study uses law-student participants. CyberCase currently binds after judgement.

claim_support.claim: LLMs have been studied as assistants for writing sections of forensic reports, with human proofreading remaining necessary in the studied setting.
claim_support.evidence: Primary arXiv abstract for the published 2024 journal article: report-structure analysis and a case study of generating report sections. CyberCase report rendering is deterministic; this work is a related application rather than the implemented rendering algorithm.

claim_support.claim: Two-stage case-specific summarization and report consolidation have prior use in digital forensics.
claim_support.evidence: Official university publication abstract: local LLMs summarize chunks of chat conversations and combine summaries into an investigative report; citation and chronology weaknesses remain. The study uses Gemini-generated reference output, not independent forensic ground truth.

claim_support.claim: A subsequent intrinsic correction pass can degrade initially correct reasoning, so preservation and correction require separate measurement.
claim_support.evidence: arXiv 2310.01798v2, section 3.3: correct-to-incorrect and incorrect-to-correct transitions; OpenReview confirms ICLR 2024 publication. Tested prompts and models do not support a universal claim about all current LLMs; CyberCase judgement is not intrinsic self-correction.

claim_support.claim: Generation, critique and correction can be evaluated separately with fixed prior responses and different critic models.
claim_support.evidence: Official abstract: 15 datasets in five reasoning domains and evaluation of generation-critique-correction capabilities, including inter-model critique. CyberCase reading/judgement is a different task decomposition and is not a CriticBench implementation.

claim_support.claim: Information preservation across LLM hand-offs can be tested using atomic ground truth and controlled injected errors.
claim_support.evidence: arXiv 2607.09678v2, sections 3-5: twelve programmatic facts, five formats and six relay hops, per-hop QA/string recall and a paired-fork injected error. Pure relay copying differs from CyberCase extraction-to-summary; preservation does not imply correction or source truth.

claim_support.claim: Iterated LLM text transmission can change measurable properties of the text.
claim_support.evidence: Abstract and experimental description: telephone-game chains track toxicity, positivity, difficulty and length. Official conference PDF confirms ICLR 2025. These measurements are not atomic case-fact preservation scores.

claim_support.claim: When to ask for clarification should be evaluated separately from producing a plausible clarifying question.
claim_support.evidence: Official abstract: a task-agnostic when-to-clarify framework and IntentSim estimate entropy over user intents, across QA, MT and NLI. CyberCase uses high-priority/askable flags and fixed budgets, not IntentSim.

claim_support.claim: Interactive systems can seek additional information under incomplete context, with question burden and downstream answer quality evaluated jointly.
claim_support.evidence: NeurIPS 2024 official abstract: a benchmark and framework for question-asking clinical reasoning under incomplete information. Clinical labels and empirical gains do not establish general-case or forensic performance.

claim_support.claim: Evaluation of missing material information should include deficient and fully specified queries to distinguish useful clarification from indiscriminate hedging.
claim_support.evidence: Primary abstract: attorney-annotated query insufficiency with eight missing-element categories and switch, gating and fatal-prerequisite modes. US legal-advice benchmark; not CyberCase's five-W-and-one-H gap taxonomy.

claim_support.claim: Missing-information detection can be evaluated against explicit expected content categories.
claim_support.evidence: Official author abstract: annotates observed behavior, expected behavior and steps to reproduce, and detects absent expected behavior/steps. Bug-report labels do not establish case-analysis readiness.

claim_support.claim: The journalistic who, what, when, where, why and how questions provide a reusable descriptive view of events.
claim_support.evidence: Primary abstract: a rule-based English news-event extractor answering 5W1H. Supports the checklist vocabulary, not CyberCase's LLM-based gap detection or a universal notion of case completeness.

claim_support.claim: Event annotations with triggers and participant roles can support role-preservation evaluation on a cybersecurity subdomain.
claim_support.evidence: AAAI official abstract and paper: cybersecurity event extraction, arguments and event coreference. CASIE is not a general-case benchmark and unmatched annotations are not automatically unsupported-source claims.

claim_support.claim: Retrieval-augmented generation conditions language generation on external non-parametric knowledge.
claim_support.evidence: NeurIPS 2020 official abstract: dense Wikipedia retrieval with parametric and non-parametric memory. Supports RAG background, not CyberCase's HTTP client's internal retriever, joint training, or an assumption that every case needs RAG.

claim_support.claim: A gate can select whether external retrieval should augment a conversational response.
claim_support.evidence: Official abstract: RAGate learns a binary adaptive-augmentation choice from human judgments. CyberCase's gate targets technical/MITRE applicability, not the same response-utility label.

claim_support.claim: XLM-R is a multilingual pretrained encoder usable as a foundation for a task-specific classifier.
claim_support.evidence: Official ACL abstract: multilingual masked-language-model pretraining over one hundred languages and cross-lingual transfer. Local config identifies XLMRobertaForSequenceClassification. This does not validate the local threshold or active deployment mode.

claim_support.claim: Attack-pattern extraction and ATT&CK mapping have published datasets and methods distinct from simple indicator extraction.
claim_support.evidence: Primary arXiv abstract for RAID 2023 publication: LADDER extracts attack patterns, maps them to ATT&CK, and releases a benchmark. Local gate.json names a LADDER sentence classifier, but that file alone does not prove a reproducible training lineage.

claim_support.claim: Document-context ATT&CK annotations can support external evaluation of a conditional technical-analysis module.
claim_support.evidence: Correct official LREC-COLING 2024 abstract at 2024.lrec-main.103: domain-expert annotation of reports, entities, time and implicit/explicit tactics/techniques linked to ATT&CK. Native annotation units need a declared rule before being converted into binary gate labels.

claim_support.claim: CTI evaluations should measure consistency and confidence as well as task accuracy.
claim_support.evidence: Primary arXiv abstract for the 2025 published book chapter: evaluations on real-size threat reports find consistency/confidence issues in the tested models. Does not imply all current LLMs or this particular pipeline are unreliable at the same rate.

claim_support.claim: A template-to-LLM rewriting pipeline is a published approach to generating CTI reports from formal entity graphs.
claim_support.evidence: Primary arXiv abstract for the IEEE Big Data 2023 paper: AGIR combines templates and an LLM over graph representations. CyberCase uses a stored case trace and deterministic projection without a report-stage LLM or a STIX entity-graph implementation.

claim_support.claim: Report evaluation can distinguish content selection, record accuracy and content ordering.
claim_support.evidence: PDF section 3.2, p. 4: content-selection, relation-generation and ordering metrics for data-to-document generation. CyberCase's deterministic renderer needs declared intended fields and projection checks rather than copying the original basketball-domain extractor.

claim_support.claim: Semantic accuracy should be assessed separately from fluency when models turn structured data into prose.
claim_support.evidence: Official ACL abstract: newly collected structured API data and human/model-based semantic-error analysis of open LLM outputs. CyberCase report rendering does not itself perform neural data-to-text generation.

claim_support.claim: Structured-output constraints can interact with task performance, so format and content correctness should be measured separately.
claim_support.evidence: Official ACL abstract: controlled structured-format versus free-form generation on several tasks and tested-model reasoning effects. This does not prove JSON harms CyberCase or that valid JSON implies semantic correctness.

claim_support.claim: Typhoon OCR is an open vision-language approach for Thai and English document extraction.
claim_support.evidence: Primary arXiv abstract: transcription, layout reconstruction and Thai-focused training. CyberCase's Typhoon HTTP recognizer establishes provider integration, not the exact serving checkpoint, OCR V1.5, or local handwriting performance.

claim_support.claim: OCR quality should be assessed through its effect on downstream language-processing tasks.
claim_support.evidence: Official author institution abstract: extrinsic evaluation of OCR errors on segmentation, entity recognition, parsing, retrieval, topic modelling and language-model fine-tuning. The study is not a modern LLM case-summarization benchmark.

claim_support.claim: Statistical tests for NLP comparisons should match the metric, experimental design and dependencies among samples.
claim_support.evidence: Official ACL abstract and paper section 3: a practical test-selection protocol; discussion of dependent language data. Supports matched case-level comparisons, not a universal requirement to use a single particular test.

claim_support.claim: A small evaluation can be underpowered and should report uncertainty and a scoped interpretation of effects.
claim_support.evidence: Official ACL abstract: NLP power analysis and underpowered automatic/human evaluation settings. Does not establish that a fixed number of CyberCase examples is automatically sufficient or insufficient.

claim_support.claim: Hosted LLM outputs may vary even under settings intended to be deterministic.
claim_support.evidence: Official workshop abstract: repeated calls to five hosted models over eight tasks and ten runs, with raw/answer agreement metrics. Observations do not measure CyberCase's provider or prove temperature-zero runs are exactly reproducible.

claim_support.claim: Clarification-question ranking can be motivated by the expected usefulness of the answer.
claim_support.evidence: Official ACL abstract: neural expected-value-of-perfect-information ranking using StackExchange question-answer pairs and expert evaluation. CyberCase chooses the first eligible gap; it does not implement or estimate neural EVPI.
